result.summary: Agency spend growth is mostly volume (about 77%), not price. A self-reinforcing loop is supported. Higher agency share raises charge and orientation load on permanent RNs, and that load precedes resignations by about two quarters. The 4 West pilot cut load, exhaustion and resignations against matched units. Resignations were rising before St. Brennan's opened, and only 19 of 98 known leavers went there. Workload is the main exit reason, and pay is secondary. The 2025 bonus did not stop vacancies rising. The CFO plan to suspend the charge and preceptor differentials would worsen the load. Extend the 4 West model. Renegotiating the escalator is a modest supplementary lever, since price explains only about 23% of the increase.

The 98.1% figure reflects a metric change, not better service. Revisions per 100 shipments jumped from about 2.9 to 14.1. The reason-code mix shifted to Operational-Capacity, late same-day revisions rose, and customer notification fell. The jumps began when the bonus took effect, in March at Northgate and Riverside and in July at Pell Junction. RouteWise timing doesn't fit: Northgate jumped before it had RouteWise, and Pell Junction had it but didn't jump until July. Brightwell's dock logs show 81% on time against the original date, down from 87%, while the scorecard claimed 98.4%. Lateness complaints rose while damage and billing complaints were flat. Suspend the claim, audit the revisions and re-base the incentive. The driver-shortage link is unestablished.

The yield decline is real: the CMM measurement system is stable (E4) and the FPY definition is unchanged (E2). The new-operator hypothesis is contradicted, because FPY fell before they ran alone and their reject rate matches the experienced operators' (E14). Three causes remain confounded. These are the Corvane hardness spread, spindle wear after the deferred service (L3-02 and L3-05 are over the runout limit), and 12-hour-shift fatigue. Lot sequence, service deferral and shift change all overlap in time, and the defect codes cannot tell them apart (E12). Scrap tag times do not give the hour a part was cut (E3). The backlog pressure to defer service is documented (E9, E16). Reverting shifts, cancelling Corvane, penalizing operators or cutting inspection would each be premature or harmful. The staggered service with trial lots and hour-of-machining recovery (A2) best separates the causes. The Line 6 Corvane CMM results (X6) would also help.

Ticket records show Arts is not deprioritised: category- and priority-matched Arts tickets are within 0.3 days of others, and on-site hardware delays match Education at the same campus (Tue/Thu technician coverage). SlotBook tickets, auto-routed to P4 by RR-17 with a 21-day median, account for 70% of the resolution gap. SlotBook explains 42% of Arts tickets, but non-SlotBook volume is still 1.6x average, so it does not fully explain the volume. The acknowledgement template hides best-effort status. Whether Arts leadership was told of RR-17 is undocumented, and the SSO link to the SlotBook rise is unproven. Fix the support status and the acknowledgement, and monitor; do not impose P4 on all Arts tickets, decommission SlotBook, or transfer budget yet.

The FY2026 record came from the commodity price rally, not from operations. Revenue rose 46.5% while bushels fell 0.9%. Peers with no new program grew revenue 41%, and Cottonwood Prairie ranks 10th of 23 on net savings growth. The 6% cost-per-bushel gain comes entirely from maintenance cut from $905K to $612K, while the deferred backlog tripled to $1.26M. Harlan Junction has critical insurer findings, including a disconnected bearing sensor and a near-miss closed without the required investigation. Staff report that nothing changes after near-misses, not fear of reprisal. Drying and grading depend on an undocumented, retiring superintendent with no successor. The expansion proposal rests on FY2026 prices, an unsupported volume assumption, and staffing and maintenance plans marked "to follow". Fix the safety issues, start succession, and rebuild the financial case before voting.

System records show first-contact demand up only 4%, while agent-created split tickets (240 to 3,710), customer duplicates and reopens exploded after the per-agent quota began. Closes per agent rose, so effort is not the issue. Headcount and hours are flat. The reopen trigger and report are unchanged, so the reopen rise is not an artifact. The quota-exempt Billing pod stayed stable, which acts as a natural control. Payroll adds about 380 first-contact tickets a month, too few to explain the backlog. Resignations are confounded by the pay deferral and a competitor offering 15% more. The Engineering bug contribution is unresolved. Suspend the per-agent quota and classify the aged tickets. Adding agents or raising the quota would worsen things.

The 98% figure is largely an artifact of date revision, not improved service. Revisions per 100 shipments rose 5x after the bonus took effect, at Northgate and Riverside in March and at Pell Junction in July. Reason codes shifted from customer request to operational capacity, and late and unnotified revisions increased. Brightwell's dock log shows 81% on time against the original date, down from 87%, while the scorecard said 98.4%. Dispatchers report pressure to protect the number. RouteWise timing and weather do not fit. The complaint rise is not explained by the portal. The driver shortage is unestablished. Suspend the claim, recompute against original dates, re-base the incentive, and do not launch the campaign, raise the bonus or fund the hiring plan yet.

The backlog growth is driven by the quota, not demand, effort or capacity. First-contact issues rose only 4%, while split children rose from 240 to 3,710, duplicates from 410 to 2,770, and reopens from 6% to 23%. A quick-wins filter appeared three days after the quota and now covers 41% of picks. The unquota'd Billing-Compliance pod stayed flat. Headcount and hours are about unchanged. The audit log and Team C's results show the reopen rise is real, not an artifact. Payroll adds only about 380 first-contact tickets a month and 210 backlog tickets. Resignations are confounded by Corvane's pay offer and the deferred pay review. Replace the per-agent quota with quality measures and classify the aged complex tickets. Do not raise the quota or hire yet.

The 30% decline is mostly a regional trend (peers -29%) plus a venue shock. The move to Brightwater cut seats 40%, with poor transit and late-concert access. Single-ticket sales fell 45% against a peer median of -9%, and the cathedral near the rail station sold far better. The music director's repertoire is not the driver: post-1945 concerts sell the same as others at Brightwater, and loyal subscribers renew at a steady 85%. Marketing impact is unestablished because no attribution exists. Do not non-renew citing revenue or cut new music. Present a segmented analysis, separate the artistic review, use the cathedral dates and a shuttle. Hold off on replacing the marketing agency.

Agency spend growth is about 77% volume and 23% rate, so the market-price framing is mostly wrong. Vacancies and resignations began climbing in 2024, before St. Brennan's opened, and only 19 of 98 known leavers went there. The 4 West pilot, with matched controls and unchanged pay, cut charge and orientation load, exhaustion and resignations, which supports the self-reinforcing loop. The 2025 bonus did not reduce vacancies. The proposed $15,000 bonus would suspend charge and preceptor differentials while adding preceptor load, which is harmful. Extending the 4 West model is the preferred action. Rate renegotiation is acceptable but secondary. Falls evidence is confounded. Time-to-hire is unestablished.

Evidence does not show ITS deprioritising Arts. SlotBook tickets (42% of Arts volume, all routed to P4 best-effort under RR-17) explain about 70% of the 6-day resolution gap. Matched non-SlotBook Arts tickets are within 0.3 days of other faculties. Remaining delay comes from Tuesday/Thursday-only Lindqvist on-site coverage. Duplicate and how-to rates are normal, so trivial tickets do not drive volume. Non-SlotBook volume is still 1.6x average, so SlotBook does not fully explain it. The P4 acknowledgement hides best-effort status. Whether Arts leadership was told of RR-17 is unestablished: the 2025-08-12 meeting has no record. Fix support status and acknowledgements and report split metrics. Do not move the desk budget or decommission SlotBook yet.

The ED length-of-stay rise is almost entirely boarding (about 3.0 of 3.2 hours), not ED work-up time. ED nurse staffing hours per visit, vacancy and grid compliance are flat, so understaffing is contradicted. Bed counts and occupancy are unchanged. Boarding jumped when the March 2026 rounding change took effect. Medical-ward discharges moved later, while surgical wards were unchanged. The 4 West huddle pilot halved boarding on huddle days, and the comparability check ruled out volume and rotation confounds. Door-to-provider and left-without-being-seen rose after the triage provider was cut on 1 May, so that link stays association-only. The September evening bed-cleaning cut is unmeasured. Extend the huddle. Do not defer case managers or pause the pilot.
